name: Project management
description: Workspaces and projects for planning and tracking work: tasks/issues with statuses and dependencies, kanban boards, sprints/cycles, milestones, time tracking, comments, and reporting.

sources.title: Plane
sources.notes: reference-only (AGPL). Modern issue-tracking/project-management app (Linear/Jira-like). Cloned apps/api (Django backend) from the `preview` branch. Covers Workspace, Project, Issue (+ Assignee/Label/Comment/Attachment/Relation/Subscriber/Reaction/Version), State/StateGroup, Cycle, Module, Estimate, View, Page, Intake, Notification models.

sources.title: Kanboard
sources.notes: Permissive (MIT). A focused, mature kanban board tool (PHP). Full repository cloned (76 MB, under the 200,000 KB threshold). TaskModel/SubtaskModel/ColumnModel/SwimlaneModel/BoardModel/ProjectModel/ProjectRoleModel are the primary references. This is the domain's permissively-licensed source, per the research brief's request to find one where possible.

sources.title: Redmine
sources.license: GPL-2.0 or later (LICENSE.txt, "either version 2 of the License, or any later version")
sources.notes: Inspected via `gh api` (not cloned; GPL-2.0, reference-only). Long-established Ruby on Rails issue tracker. IssueStatus (is_closed flag, default_done_ratio) with per-tracker/per-role WorkflowTransition rules; IssueRelation with TYPE_RELATES/DUPLICATES/DUPLICATED/BLOCKS/BLOCKED/PRECEDES/FOLLOWS/COPIED_TO/COPIED_FROM and explicit reverse-type pairs; Version with VERSION_STATUSES (open/locked/closed) and VERSION_SHARINGS; Project.is_public boolean visibility. OpenProject is a fork of Redmine (via ChiliProject), so the two are NOT treated as fully independent lineages for corroboration counting; noted per-feature where this matters.

sources.title: OpenProject
sources.notes: Inspected via `gh api` (not cloned; GPL-3.0, reference-only). Full project/portfolio management suite (Ruby on Rails, forked from Redmine via ChiliProject). Status model with workflow transitions; Version (VERSION_STATUSES open/locked/closed, effective_date, sharing); a dedicated `resource_management` module (allocation_step, assignment_candidate, schedule_violation components) for workload/capacity planning; a relation-driven auto-scheduling engine (WorkPackages::ScheduleDependency, DependencyGraph, SetScheduleService) for Gantt date propagation; a dedicated `webhooks` module with outgoing delivery logs; OAuth applications/clients for API access; documented GitHub/GitLab integrations with webhook secrets.

sources.title: Vikunja
sources.notes: Inspected via `gh api` (not cloned; AGPL-3.0, reference-only). Go/Vue task manager. Kanban Bucket with a numeric Limit field (WIP limit) and a DoneBucketID; TaskRelation RelationKind (subtask/parenttask/related/duplicateof/duplicates/blocking/blocked/precedes/follows/copiedfrom/copiedto); TaskRepeatMode (default/monthly/from-current-date) with RepeatAfter seconds, applied to the SAME task (reopens it and bumps dates) rather than spawning a new task; IsFavorite per user; SavedFilters; a dedicated Webhook model (target URL, configurable event list, HMAC signing, Basic Auth); a `pkg/caldav` CalDAV server; a `pkg/modules/migration` package with real importers for Trello, Todoist, TickTick, Wekan, Planka, Microsoft To Do, and CSV.

sources.title: Focalboard
sources.license: AGPL-3.0 (source) or commercial; MIT applies ONLY to compiled binaries produced by Mattermost, and Apache-2.0 only to webapp/html-templates/, app-config.json, config.json, webapp/i18n/, server/model/ and plugin/
sources.notes: **Reference-only. The license was recorded as plain MIT in an earlier pass and that was wrong.** Read directly from LICENSE.txt at the pinned ref: the *source code* is licensed under AGPL-3.0 (with a narrow non-enforcement promise) or a commercial license from Mattermost; the MIT grant covers only compiled versions that Mattermost itself produces, and Apache-2.0 covers only the listed admin/config directories. GitHub's API reports NOASSERTION for exactly this reason. Never copy code from it into the kit. Go/TS kanban-board tool (a Trello-like product originally by Mattermost). Board with BoardType (Open/Private) and a block-based content model (BlockType: board/card/view/text/checkbox/comment/image/attachment/divider); a Sharing model exposing a board via an access-token public link, distinct from workspace membership.

sources.title: Leantime
sources.notes: Inspected via `gh api` (not cloned; AGPL-3.0, reference-only). PHP project/goal-management tool aimed at non-technical teams. Tickets.statusListSeed defines configurable per-status labels grouped by a `statusType` of NEW/INPROGRESS/DONE (a second, independently-built grouped-status model alongside Plane's StateGroup); Tickets.efforts is a Fibonacci-like point scale (0.5/1/2/3/5/8/13 -> XS..XXL); Tickets.type includes a literal 'milestone' type (a milestone is a Ticket row, with its own getAllMilestones() timeline query, headline, and color) rather than a separate Milestone model; Sprints model (name/startDate/endDate/projectId); Timesheets records hours/description plus independent invoicedEmpl/invoicedComp boolean+date pairs (employee-side vs company-side invoicing), a manual-entry-plus-billing model distinct from Kanboard's timer-based one.

sources.title: Taiga (backend)
sources.notes: Inspected via `gh api` (not cloned; MPL-2.0 per its own LICENSE file -- weak/file-level copyleft, more permissive than AGPL/GPL but not promoted into the kit as permissive). Django/Python agile project-management backend. Epic model (own EpicStatus FK, epics_order, color) distinct from and above user stories; Milestone (Sprint) model with estimated_start/estimated_finish and closed_points/total_closed_points_by_date -- a real burndown-data computation, not just date fields.

sources.title: The Scrum Guide (2020 edition)
sources.license: Publicly published by scrumguides.org (brand-neutral, maintained by Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland)
sources.notes: The authoritative definition of Scrum. Used only for what it actually specifies: the Sprint as a fixed-length timebox that starts immediately after the previous Sprint ends, Sprint Planning/Daily Scrum/Sprint Review/Sprint Retrospective, Product Backlog refinement (breaking down and adding detail/order/size to backlog items), Sprint cancellation authority, Sprint Backlog/Product Backlog/Increment/Definition of Done. The 2020 edition deliberately dropped prescriptive artifacts like burndown charts, so it is NOT cited as authority for burndown/velocity reporting.

sources.title: ISO 21502:2020 -- Project, programme and portfolio management -- Guidance on project management
sources.license: ISO copyright; scope/abstract freely accessible, full text is a paid standard
sources.version: ISO 21502:2020 (first edition); supersedes the project-management guidance content of ISO 21500:2012
sources.notes: General, tool-agnostic project-management terminology (project governance, milestones, schedule, deliverables) used only for the domain's broad framing, not for any tool-specific feature shape -- ISO 21502 does not define kanban, sprints, or any of this domain's software-specific concepts.

sources.title: A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide) -- Seventh Edition
sources.license: PMI copyright; FAQs/summary freely accessible, full text requires PMI membership or purchase
sources.notes: General project-management terminology (milestone, schedule, deliverable, stakeholder) used only for domain framing. The 7th Edition is principles-and-performance-domain based, not process-based, and does not define any software-tracker-specific feature.

sources.title: The Official Guide to The Kanban Method
sources.notes: The published definition of the Kanban Method (David J. Anderson): Visualize the workflow, Limit WIP, Manage flow, Make policies explicit, Implement feedback loops, Improve collaboratively/evolve experimentally. Directly grounds this domain's kanban board + WIP-limit capability as an authoritative, not just tool-convention, concept.

sources.title: RFC 6749 -- The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework
sources.notes: The standard authorization framework third-party integrations (public API access, OAuth apps) commonly use; OpenProject implements OAuth applications/clients for its API, cited alongside this RFC rather than as a substitute for it.

sources.title: RFC 4791 -- Calendaring Extensions to WebDAV (CalDAV)
sources.notes: The standard protocol for calendar sync; Vikunja implements a CalDAV server (pkg/caldav) that this domain's calendar_sync integration is modeled on.

features.name: Workspaces
features.description: A top-level container for an organization's projects, members, and settings.

provenance.notes: Plane's Workspace/WorkspaceMember/WorkspaceTheme models remain the only source found for a tenant-level container ABOVE projects. Checked and ruled out as corroboration: Kanboard (no layer above project), OpenProject/Redmine (projects can nest under a parent project but there is no separate workspace/tenant entity), Vikunja (removed its Namespace model in favor of self-nesting Projects via ParentProjectID), Leantime (a 'Program' grouping exists but only via its optional PgmPro plugin, not core). Left at low confidence honestly rather than treating a plugin or a project-nesting mechanism as equivalent.

features.name: Projects
features.description: A container for a related set of tasks, with its own members, states, and settings, inside a workspace.

provenance.notes: Plane's Project/ProjectMember/ProjectIdentifier models and Kanboard's ProjectModel/ProjectRoleModel are independent implementations.

features.name: Tasks / issues
features.description: The core unit of work: a title, description, assignees, priority, dates, and status, belonging to a project.

provenance.notes: Plane's Issue model (priority, start_date/target_date, assignees, sequence_id) and Kanboard's TaskModel (is_active open/closed, priority, due date) are independent implementations.

features.name: Subtasks
features.description: Breaking a task down into smaller child tasks tracked toward the parent's completion.

provenance.notes: Plane's Issue.parent self-referencing ForeignKey and Kanboard's dedicated SubtaskModel (a distinct, lighter-weight checklist-style subtask, not a full task) are independent implementations of related but differently-scoped concepts.

features.name: Statuses and workflows
features.description: Configurable per-project statuses (grouped into backlog/unstarted/started/completed/cancelled) that define a task's workflow.

provenance.notes: Plane's State/StateGroup (backlog/unstarted/started/completed/cancelled/triage) and Leantime's statusListSeed (configurable per-status labels grouped by a statusType of NEW/INPROGRESS/DONE) are independently-built implementations of the same idea: per-project configurable statuses grouped into a small set of lifecycle buckets. Redmine's IssueStatus/WorkflowTransition and OpenProject's Status model add per-tracker/role transition RULES on top of a similar configurable-status base, but OpenProject is a fork of Redmine (via ChiliProject) so the two are not counted as a third independent source here -- noted as consistent, not tallied.

features.name: Kanban boards
features.description: A visual board of columns (statuses) and swimlanes, with drag-and-drop task cards.

provenance.notes: Kanboard's dedicated BoardModel/ColumnModel/SwimlaneModel (with WIP-limit-oriented ColumnRestrictionModel) is the direct implementation; Plane's State.sequence + Issue.sort_order corroborate the same board/column concept from a second source.

features.name: Task dependencies
features.description: Linking tasks with typed relations (blocks, relates to, duplicates, must-start/finish-before) to sequence work.

provenance.notes: Three independently-built implementations converge on the same typed, bidirectional relation taxonomy: Plane's IssueRelationChoices (blocked_by/blocking, relates_to, duplicate, start_before/finish_before, implemented_by), Vikunja's RelationKind (blocking/blocked, related, duplicateof/duplicates, precedes/follows, subtask/parenttask, copiedfrom/copiedto), and Redmine's IssueRelation TYPE_* constants (blocks/blocked, relates, duplicates/duplicated, precedes/follows, copied_to/copied_from) with explicit reverse-type pairs. All three independently chose the same blocks/relates/duplicates/precedes+reverse-pair shape.

features.name: Comments and mentions
features.description: Threaded discussion on a task, with @-mentions and emoji reactions.

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations: Plane's IssueComment/IssueMention/CommentReaction, Kanboard's CommentModel (with a dedicated comment.user.mention event), and Vikunja's task_comments.go plus mentions.go (FindMentionedUsersInText). Emoji/comment reactions specifically are only confirmed in Plane; the core comment+@mention pattern is confirmed in all three.

features.name: Cycles / sprints
features.description: A fixed-duration iteration (sprint) that a set of tasks is planned into and executed within.

provenance.notes: Plane's Cycle model (start_date/end_date, owned_by, CycleIssue join) and Leantime's Sprints model (name/startDate/endDate/projectId) are two independent implementations of a fixed-duration iteration. The Scrum Guide (2020) is authoritative for the underlying concept it calls a Sprint: a fixed-length timebox that starts immediately after the previous one ends and can be cancelled (only by the Product Owner) if its goal becomes obsolete -- note the state NAMES used in this domain's cycle entity (upcoming/active/completed/cancelled) are Plane's, not verbatim Scrum Guide terminology.

features.name: Modules / epics
features.description: A larger unit of work (feature or epic) that groups related tasks, independent of the sprint/cycle timeline.

provenance.notes: Plane's Module model (ModuleStatus: backlog/planned/in-progress/paused/completed/cancelled) and Taiga's Epic model (its own EpicStatus foreign key, ordering, color) are independent implementations of a larger, cross-iteration grouping of work above individual tasks/stories.

features.name: Milestones
features.description: A target date marking a significant point in a project, used to group and track progress toward a deliverable.

provenance.notes: No dedicated 'Milestone' model exists in Plane (the earlier single-source, reasoned mapping onto Module has been dropped from provenance). Three independent implementations of a real milestone concept: Leantime models a milestone as a Ticket with type='milestone' (its own headline, tags/color, and a dedicated getAllMilestones() timeline query); Redmine's Version (effective_date, VERSION_STATUSES open/locked/closed, VERSION_SHARINGS); OpenProject's Version (same VERSION_STATUSES/effective_date shape, inherited from the Redmine lineage but re-verified independently in OpenProject's own model file). Because Redmine and OpenProject share code lineage, this is treated as two-plus-one rather than three fully unrelated codebases, but the Leantime + Redmine/OpenProject combination is still a genuine, independently converged 'milestone/version has an open/locked/closed-like lifecycle and a target date' shape.

features.name: Gantt / timeline view
features.description: A horizontal timeline view of tasks by start/target date, showing dependencies and overlaps.

provenance.notes: Plane's Issue.start_date/target_date plus IssueRelationChoices (start_before/finish_before) is a reasoned basis for a client-side Gantt view. OpenProject's WorkPackages::ScheduleDependency / DependencyGraph / SetScheduleService is a concrete, dedicated relation-driven automatic-rescheduling engine -- a second, independently-built and considerably more developed implementation of dependency-aware date computation for a Gantt/timeline view.

features.name: Time tracking
features.description: Logging time spent on a task, by whom and when, for effort reporting.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations with genuinely different capture models: Kanboard's SubtaskTimeTrackingModel (start/stop timer per subtask, computed duration) and Leantime's Timesheets (manual workDate/hours/description entry, a billable/not-billable 'kind', and independent invoicedEmpl/invoicedComp boolean+date pairs for employee-side vs company-side invoicing).

features.name: Labels
features.description: Free-form or predefined tags applied to tasks for categorization and filtering.

provenance.notes: Plane's Label/IssueLabel models and Kanboard's TaskTagModel/category+color model are independent implementations.

features.name: Attachments
features.description: Uploading files to a task for reference (screenshots, documents, designs).

provenance.notes: Plane's IssueAttachment/Asset models and Kanboard's TaskFileModel are independent implementations.

features.name: Saved views and filters
features.description: Saving a combination of filters, sort order, and grouping as a reusable view.

provenance.notes: Plane's View model and Vikunja's SavedFilters (saved_filters.go, a first-class, persisted, reusable filter/sort/grouping definition distinct from a one-off request-time filter) are independent implementations.

features.name: Guest / client access
features.description: A restricted external member role for clients or stakeholders to view or comment on specific projects without full workspace access.

provenance.notes: Plane's ProjectPublicMember/ProjectDeployBoard remains the only source found for a restricted, role-based external member. Checked and ruled out: Focalboard's Sharing model is a public access-TOKEN link for a board (no distinct guest role or membership), which is a closer match to this domain's view-sharing feature than to a guest role, so it was applied there instead rather than double-counted here.

features.name: Activity feed
features.description: A chronological, per-task or per-project audit trail of field changes, status moves, and comments.

provenance.notes: Plane's IssueActivity model and Kanboard's project/task activity analytics (ProjectActivityModel, TaskEventBuilder) are independent implementations.

features.name: Estimates / story points
features.description: Sizing a task's effort, either as a raw point value or against a project-defined estimate scale.

provenance.notes: Plane's Issue.point (raw 0-12) / Issue.estimate_point (FK to a project-defined Estimate scale) and Leantime's Tickets.efforts (a Fibonacci-like point scale, 0.5/1/2/3/5/8/13 mapped to XS..XXL labels) are independent implementations of a project-configurable effort-sizing scale.

features.name: Recurring tasks
features.description: Automatically regenerating a task on a schedule once the previous occurrence is completed.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations that use genuinely different mechanisms: Kanboard's TaskRecurrenceModel / RecurringTaskSubscriber spawns a NEW task instance when the original is completed, while Vikunja's RepeatAfter/RepeatMode (default interval / monthly / from-current-date) instead reopens and bumps the dates on the SAME task. Both are cited, and the difference is treated as two valid implementation strategies rather than collapsed into one.

features.name: Workload / capacity view
features.description: Visualizing how much work is assigned to each person to spot over/under-allocation.

provenance.notes: Plane's Issue.assignees plus per-user CycleUserProperties/ModuleUserProperties is a reasoned basis for a per-assignee load view. OpenProject ships a dedicated `resource_management` module (allocation-step components, assignment-candidate matching, schedule-violation warnings, working-hours awareness) -- a second, independently-built and considerably more developed implementation of workload/capacity planning.

features.name: Burndown and velocity reports
features.description: Charting remaining work over a cycle (burndown) and completed points per cycle over time (velocity).

provenance.notes: Plane's Cycle + CycleIssue + Issue.estimate_point/point is a reasoned basis for computing burndown/velocity. Taiga's Milestone model concretely computes this: estimated_start/estimated_finish plus closed_points/total_closed_points_by_date is a real burndown-data method, a second independent implementation. Note the Scrum Guide (2020) is NOT cited here -- it deliberately dropped prescriptive burndown-chart language in its 2020 revision, so it is not authority for this feature.

features.name: View sharing
features.description: Sharing a saved view publicly or with specific teammates.

provenance.notes: Plane's View model combined with its ProjectDeployBoard public-sharing pattern, and Focalboard's Sharing model (a board exposed via an access-token public link, toggled on/off, independent of workspace membership) are independent implementations of the same public-link-sharing idea.

features.name: Intake / triage
features.description: A lightweight submission form (often for non-members) that creates a triage-state task for a maintainer to accept or reject.

provenance.notes: Plane's Intake model and dedicated StateGroup.TRIAGE value remain the only source found for a lightweight, often-external submission-to-triage-queue flow. Not found in Kanboard, Redmine, OpenProject, Vikunja, Focalboard, Leantime, or Taiga in the areas inspected -- left at low confidence rather than treating ordinary issue creation as equivalent to a dedicated intake/triage flow.

features.name: Favorites / pinning
features.description: Letting a user pin frequently-used projects, views, or tasks for quick access.

provenance.notes: Plane's Favorite model and Vikunja's per-user IsFavorite field (with dedicated favorites-access-scoped search handling) are independent implementations.

features.name: Private projects
features.description: Restricting a project's visibility to explicitly invited members within the workspace.

provenance.notes: Plane's ProjectNetwork enum (private/public) and Redmine's Project.is_public boolean (with matching visibility-scoping query logic for anonymous/authenticated users) are independent implementations of project-level visibility control.
